blocks: The opportunity
What if the garden could give your home another room?
Not an extension of the house. A building of its own, at the end of the garden, for a use the house no longer has room for.
Illustrative diagram by PlotNua. Not to scale.
Explore the makers
The problem
The house may no longer provide enough space.
Work A desk at the kitchen table, every day.
Family Children who need somewhere loud, and parents who need somewhere quiet.
Guests and hobbies A spare room that is never spare.
The usual answers Move house, or extend the one you are living in.
The possibility
What could stand at the end of the garden?
Three kinds of building, and they are not the same project.
And one that is neither
A home in the garden that would be sold, subdivided or lived in apart from the main house is an independent dwelling. It falls outside the 2026 exemption, so it needs planning permission.
What exists today
What exists today.
Real makers and real products, and what their published prices do and do not tell you.
The practicalities
The practicalities.
What the regulations require, kept apart from our practical guidance.
What the regulations require
From the Planning and Development (Exempted Development) Regulations 2026, in operation since 27 July 2026, and the Building Control rules.
Practical guidance
PlotNua’s reading of the requirements, for a first look at your own garden. It is not legal advice.
25 m² kept for the house, 5 m × 5 m, say
Garden home 32–45 m², about 5.7 m square
≥ 0.6 m from the boundary
A way in on foot , no new entrance onto the road
